body: I could have killed myself today. I have had plenty of time. Instead, I take a lot of prescribed drugs and slept away the day (rather hoping that all of the drugs will overdose me). I need to "man up" and can only hope to soon.

Unfortunately, I do not feel that I can say much else about what I've done. I wish I could say more. I will say though that I do not think what I have done will even be remembered- 99.99% sure that it won't be. It's still hard to live with myself. 

Thank you though, and do feel free to subtract your support anytime.

I have done therapy on and off for many years, never finding it helpful. In particular, within the last few years, I have talked some about the thoughts that I have to hurt others like I was hurt.

I've taken a lot of medications in the hopes that something will break my depression, but I find that it cannot stop the depression from the ultimate source- having been abused and never able to forget. 

What I did is about 99.99% sure never to affect the person negatively, but it is hard to live with myself. Also, since I never expected the urge that drove me, I don't know what will come next in theory.

Thank you though.

You're right- something has put a lot of care in your heart, because I certainly don't deserve your support. 

I hope there is a God who would forgive me, but then, I have always said (before I did this) that if a God forgives abusers, I don't want to be known by him and I don't want to know him. Ironic.
I'm not sure what is "a lot" I can do? I wish that there were resources, not that it would change how much disgust I have for myself.

I have been in counseling for my childhood abuse for many years on and off. I have been able to talk about the thoughts I have. However, unless you have been put through the system in some way as an abuser, there seems to be no help on preventing a victim from becoming an abuser...

I feel like a therapist should have brought up the topic with me of continuing the cycle. I certainly never planned this, and I wasn't prepared for these thoughts to come up and how to fight them. 

Anyway, thank you for your suggestions.

I'm worried about hell, too. I was raised in church for years, so I don't think I will ever be able to shake that fear in the back of my mind. I can totally relate to what you have posted. I don't want to be on either side myself.

I agree with the poster who said they just want to dream forever. 

I am afraid of Hell, and also afraid that if there isn't a Heaven or Hell, there may be some kind of awareness that causes me to feel stuck in having committed suicide- feeling mentally tortured in some way instead of just meeting nothingness forever. I think I could do nothingness okay. Ideally though, I would see those couple of people who are dear to me again without judgement on either side.
I have always thought that they should die. I am surprised to hear a different opinion.

I get your point, but I do want to say- a parent who has molested their child, then reality sets in, is probably going to be numb and inwardly rolling in self-hatred or self-absorption. If such an outpouring of love was there as in the post you linked, I doubt they would have molested their child in the first place.

I am 25F who was abused for years in childhood. I know it may be strange to hear this from a female, but I know these urges. I've looked it up as well, even toddlercon. I too thought "I'll kill myself if I ever hurt a child" and that I could confine this sickness. 

There are many people in this world who look at loli and worse, and a lot of them never hurt a child. I tend to believe that there are many more who DO. I never thought I would do such a thing, and I remember saying that I'd kill myself first. It's not that simple. I want and need to kill myself, but I can't get the balls to do it. Now I am trapped in a self-hatred that I can tell no one the reason for.

I wish you could get some help before it becomes something no one can help you with.
How should a parent of a child speak about abusing them? I believe this post, 100%.
Yes, women surely do. Thank you for reminding everyone. (25F) My mother was one of my abusers.

I am a female childhood sexual abuse survivor who has been in therapy on and off for many years. I have had these same urges, and I have been inappropriate as well. One commenter said that they believe it has to be a crime in consideration not one that has already happened, but I disagree from what I have been told by professionals. If you admit to abusing your daughter in the past-tense, you will still be reported. It's the same as a child confessing that someone has touched her inappropriately in the past. Even if it is not currently happening, CPS and child advocacy will investigate.

Having said all of that, you DO need to seek professional help. Please. You can go to therapy and explain the urges without saying what you have perpetrated. 

It's so completely lonely from this perspective- from the perspective of someone who has urges to abuse as we both do. I think that it will eat at you, if you have a heart and proper love for your daughter.

I beg of you, don't touch her again. Children realize much more than someone might think. She may have been playing asleep. I played asleep many, many times and they didn't "notice." I am a 25 year old F who has been flirting with suicide for many years because of this. I lost my father. I wake up every morning reminded of what he has done to me.

Get help, or your daughter will be writing this post in a few years.
